$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{7-3x}{2} & >2 \\ 2\cdot (\frac{7-3x}{2}) & >2\cdot 2 \\ \cancel{2}\cdot (\frac{7-3x}{\cancel{2}}) & >2\cdot 2 \\ 7-3x & >4\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we apply the addition and multiplication principles. 

Remember, when we divide an inequality by a negative number, we need to flip the inequality sign:

$$
\begin{aligned}7-3x & >4 \\ 7-3x-7 & >4-7 \\ -3x & >-3 \\ \frac{-3x}{-3} & \,\,<\,\,\frac{-3}{-3} \\ x & <1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x<1.$

Remember, when we divide an inequality by a negative number, we need to flip the inequality sign:

$$
\begin{aligned}3x+18 & >8x \\ 3x+18-8x & >8x-8x \\ 18-5x & >0 \\ 18-5x-18 & >0-18 \\ -5x & >-18 \\ \frac{-5x}{-5} & \,\,<\,\,\frac{-18}{-5} \\ x & <\frac{18}{5}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x<\frac{18}{5}.$
